correctness.rationale: All six minimal zero-sum multisets in the cyclic residue group of order four are exhausted by the three possible presence cases of a weight-2 residue. The exact length formula 4ℓ=a+b+2c+2w, fixed parity of w, and a four-way split on atom counts prove the iff criterion for all x. The four explicit atom identities prove sufficiency; the minimum-prime bounds give least x=75411; the standalone exact checker corroborates 735 profiles and 19999 direct monoid factorizations. Finite evidence is not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Direct inspection of arXiv:2610.36284v1 section 7.5 distinguishes the published global half-factoriality classification and 194481 witness from the new elementwise four-pattern criterion and least ratio 75411. The 2007 ACM theory and Baginski–Chapman survey give a general transfer to zero-sum sequences, without the explicit first-case criterion. arXiv:2210.01224 calculates length density and other factorization invariants rather than the claimed four-threshold classification. Six actual semantic-index searches and targeted public text searches disclosed no dominating theorem; the possibility of an older implicit C4 classification is an explicit residual risk.
residual_risks: A classical C4 block-monoid classification or unindexed arithmetic-congruence-monoid table could implicitly contain the same four threshold profiles and the least example; this would alter historical originality.
The published transfer theorem makes the method standard; novelty is limited to the explicit complete heptagonal specialization and its sharp first numerical obstruction.
